questions.scenario: The table shows the percentage of dark moths in a population of peppered moths in an industrial area, where soot from factories darkened the tree trunks.
questions.scenarioAf: Die tabel toon die persentasie donker motte in ’n bevolking peper-en-soutmotte in ’n nywerheidsgebied, waar roet van fabrieke die boomstamme donker gemaak het.

questions.q: What percentage of the moths were dark in 1890?
questions.qAf: Watter persentasie van die motte was in 1890 donker?

questions.q: Describe the trend shown by the data.
questions.qAf: Beskryf die neiging wat die data toon.
points: The percentage of dark moths increased
from 2% in 1850 to 95% in 1930
pointsAf: Die persentasie donker motte het toegeneem
van 2% in 1850 tot 95% in 1930

questions.q: Use the theory of natural selection to explain this trend.
questions.qAf: Gebruik die teorie van natuurlike seleksie om hierdie neiging te verduidelik.
points: There was variation: some moths were light and some dark
on the dark trunks the light moths were easily seen and eaten by birds
the dark moths were camouflaged, so more survived and reproduced
they passed the allele for dark colour to their offspring, so the proportion of dark moths increased
pointsAf: Daar was variasie: sommige motte was lig en sommige donker
op die donker stamme is die ligte motte maklik gesien en deur voëls geëet
die donker motte was gekamoefleer, dus het meer oorleef en voortgeplant
hulle het die alleel vir donker kleur aan hul nakomelinge oorgedra, dus het die verhouding donker motte toegeneem

questions.q: After clean-air laws were passed, the percentage of light moths increased again. Explain why.

points: The tree trunks became lighter again
so light moths were now camouflaged and dark moths were eaten more often
pointsAf: Die boomstamme het weer ligter geword
dus was ligte motte nou gekamoefleer en donker motte is meer dikwels geëet

questions.q: Where does meiosis take place in a human female?

questions.q: Describe the events of metaphase I and anaphase I.
questions.qAf: Beskryf die gebeure van metafase I en anafase I.
points: Metaphase I: homologous chromosomes line up in pairs at the equator
in a random arrangement
Anaphase I: the spindle fibres contract and pull the homologous chromosomes apart
to opposite poles of the cell
pointsAf: Metafase I: homoloë chromosome staan in pare by die ewenaar
in ’n lukrake rangskikking
Anafase I: die spoeldrade trek saam en trek die homoloë chromosome uitmekaar
na teenoorgestelde pole van die sel

questions.q: Explain how non-disjunction during meiosis can lead to Down syndrome.
questions.qAf: Verduidelik hoe nie-disjunksie tydens meiose tot Downsindroom kan lei.
points: The chromosomes of pair 21 fail to separate in anaphase I (or the chromatids in anaphase II)
one gamete receives two copies of chromosome 21
when it is fertilised by a normal gamete
the zygote has three copies of chromosome 21 (47 chromosomes)
pointsAf: Die chromosome van paar 21 skei nie in anafase I nie (of die chromatiede in anafase II)
een gameet ontvang twee kopieë van chromosoom 21
wanneer dit deur ’n normale gameet bevrug word
het die sigoot drie kopieë van chromosoom 21 (47 chromosome)

questions.q: A storm blows some birds of a mainland population to a distant island. Describe how the island population could become a new species.

points: The two populations are geographically isolated
so there is no gene flow between them
the island has different environmental conditions (selection pressures)
natural selection acts differently on each population
over many generations they become genetically and phenotypically different
until they can no longer interbreed, even if they meet again (reproductive isolation)
pointsAf: Die twee bevolkings is geografies geïsoleer
dus is daar geen geenvloei tussen hulle nie
die eiland het ander omgewingstoestande (seleksiedruk)

oor baie geslagte word hulle geneties en fenotipies verskillend
totdat hulle nie meer kan kruisteel nie, selfs al ontmoet hulle weer (reproduktiewe isolasie)

questions.q:
Describe the process of DNA replication, and explain how the events of meiosis lead to genetically different gametes.
Content: 17 Synthesis: 3
NOTE: NO marks will be awarded for answers in the form of flow charts, tables or diagrams.
questions.qAf:
Beskryf die proses van DNS-replikasie, en verduidelik hoe die gebeure van meiose tot geneties verskillende gamete lei.
Inhoud: 17 Sintese: 3
LET WEL: GEEN punte sal toegeken word vir antwoorde in die vorm van vloeidiagramme, tabelle of diagramme nie.
points:
DNA replication (max 7)
It takes place in the nucleus during interphase
the DNA double helix unwinds
the weak hydrogen bonds between the bases break
the two strands separate (unzip)
each strand acts as a template
free nucleotides attach to the complementary bases
A pairs with T and C pairs with G
enzymes control the process
two identical DNA molecules form
each has one original and one new strand

Meiosis and variation (max 10)
In prophase I homologous chromosomes pair up
chromatids of homologous chromosomes overlap at points called chiasmata
crossing over takes place: segments of genetic material are exchanged
this produces new combinations of alleles on the chromatids
in metaphase I the homologous pairs line up randomly at the equator
so the chromosomes are sorted independently into the daughter cells (independent assortment)
this gives many possible combinations of chromosomes in the gametes
in metaphase II the chromosomes again line up randomly
four haploid gametes form that are genetically different from each other
random fertilisation of these gametes adds further variation
mutations during replication can also create new alleles
pointsAf:
DNS-replikasie (maks 7)
Dit vind tydens interfase in die kern plaas
die DNS-dubbelheliks ontrol
die swak waterstofbindings tussen die basisse breek
die twee stringe skei (ritssluiter gaan oop)
elke string dien as ’n templaat
vry nukleotiede heg aan die komplementêre basisse
A paar met T en C paar met G
ensieme beheer die proses
twee identiese DNS-molekules vorm
elkeen het een oorspronklike en een nuwe string

Meiose en variasie (maks 10)
In profase I paar homoloë chromosome
chromatiede van homoloë chromosome oorvleuel by punte wat chiasmata genoem word
oorkruising vind plaas: segmente genetiese materiaal word uitgeruil
dit lewer nuwe kombinasies van allele op die chromatiede
in metafase I staan die homoloë pare lukraak by die ewenaar
dus word die chromosome onafhanklik in die dogterselle gesorteer (onafhanklike sortering)
dit gee baie moontlike kombinasies van chromosome in die gamete
in metafase II staan die chromosome weer lukraak in ’n ry
vier haploïede gamete vorm wat geneties van mekaar verskil
lukrake bevrugting van hierdie gamete voeg verdere variasie by
mutasies tydens replikasie kan ook nuwe allele skep
